notes.s: Burnout named as an illness, then treated out loud instead of hidden.
notes.t: Written during the 2020 shutdown, when a group whose entire working life was touring suddenly had nothing on the calendar and discovered that rest felt worse than overwork. The verses are split between a rapper who cannot stop measuring himself by output and one who counts how many named disorders of the mind exist and concludes that almost nobody is exempt. The track is deliberately bright, an old-school boom-bap beat under lines about chewing yourself up for taking a day off. Fans latched onto the ending, where the stutter breaks the word for sickness apart and reassembles it as an order to drop the fear.
k: 병 is the sickness in the title, and it is also the word for a bottle. The next line, 버려 겁, throws away 겁, fear. Stuttering 병 into 벼벼벼 and 겁 into 거거거 makes the two words rhyme into each other, so the sickness and the fear become the same object you can put down. The English title splits disease into dis-ease, loss of rest, which is exactly what the Korean argues.
이 유리 같은 병이 때리지 니 머리

Both readings of 병 fire at once. An illness as fragile as glass, and a glass bottle swung at your head. Korean lyrics lean on this kind of homophone far more than English pop does, and the line is unreadable without it.
I'm ill, 그래 내가 일 그 자체
일 means work and sounds close enough to ill to carry the pun across languages. The claim is not that he does work but that he is work, which is the whole diagnosis of the verse.

The rotten rope comes from the folk tale where a brother and sister climb to the sky on a strong rope and the tiger chasing them is given the rotten one and falls. Reaching for the rotten rope means grabbing the help that was always going to give way.

vocab.note: Separately also means bottle; the song keeps both in play
The noun 불안 covers free-floating anxiety, not fear of one thing
Takes 하다; used for stress, hangovers, constipation, backlogs
겁이 많다, to have a lot of fear, is how Korean says someone is timid
Stuck after another verb it means do it off completely, often with regret
Only for schools; time off work is 휴가
